items.title: Section: Why Arhats Still Suffer Violent Deaths, and Why a Stream-Enterer May Still Have a Spouse

items.zh: 復於後二自稱歎處，所有相違前後乖反墮非理相而興謗難，謂於世間有眼見者、無眼見者、有他心智者、無他心智者，如來於此自稱歎處能為對治諸謗難中，都不見有如實因相。由是因緣，於此四處能自了知，坦然無畏，心無怯劣，無所疑慮，都無驚懼。
items.en:
Also, regarding the latter two self-praised grounds, objectors raise the charge that they contradict one another, appearing inconsistent and unreasonable.
The Tathāgata, examining every objection raised against these self-praised grounds, finds not the slightest genuine basis in any of them. By this cause and condition, regarding these four grounds, he knows himself truthfully, remaining entirely self-assured, his mind never weak, never in doubt, never afraid.

items.title: Section: Why Exactly Four, For Whom Each Is Taught, and Why the Compilers of Scripture Split What the Buddha Taught as One

items.zh: 又佛大師唯有爾所正應稱歎，謂自利行及利他行俱善圓滿。當知此中，前二稱歎自利行滿，後二稱歎利他行滿。此中如來，若自稱歎於一切法現等覺故成正等覺，當知正為等趣大乘諸菩薩故。若自稱歎一切漏盡，當知正為等趣聲聞及獨覺乘諸有情故。若復稱歎能出離道及諸障法，當知俱為等趣諸乘諸有情故。如是如來所說經句，謂我為諸菩薩、聲聞說出離道，乃至廣說。諸結集者，於所結集聲聞藏中，除菩薩言；於所結集菩薩藏中，但唯誦此菩薩之言。
items.en:
Third, showing there are only four. As the great teacher, the Buddha rightly praises only these; both the practice benefiting himself and the practice benefiting others are perfectly complete. Know that the first two praise the perfection of benefiting himself, the latter two praise the perfection of benefiting others.
Third, explaining for whose sake; first, for the Great Vehicle. If the Tathāgata praises himself for directly awakening to all phenomena and thus attaining perfect awakening, know this is specifically for guiding bodhisattvas equally progressing towards the Great Vehicle.
Second, for the other vehicles. If he praises himself for the exhaustion of all outflows, know this is specifically for guiding śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas equally towards their vehicles.
Third, for every vehicle; first, stating there is no distinction. If he praises the path of transcendence and the obstructing phenomena, know this is equally for beings of every vehicle.
Second, pointing to what the sūtras say. Thus the Tathāgata's own scriptural words: "I teach the path of transcendence for bodhisattvas and śrāvakas," and so on at length.
Third, showing the compilation. Those who compiled the śrāvaka canon omitted the word "bodhisattva"; those who compiled the bodhisattva canon recited only this word "bodhisattva."

items.title: Section: The Three Foundations of Mindfulness — Meeting Every Disciple, Obedient or Not, With Perfect Equanimity

items.zh: 如來所有三念住文，如契經說應知其相。謂諸如來，於其長夜有如是欲：如何當令諸有情類，於我善說法毘柰耶無倒行中，如實隨住。如是長夜欲樂法主化御眾時，若所希欲或遂不遂，不生雜染。由三念住略所顯故。此三念住，復由三眾差別建立。云何三眾？若彼一切一向正行，是第一眾；若彼一切一向邪行，是第二眾；若彼眾中一分正行、一分邪行，是第三眾。
items.en:
Fifth, the three foundations of mindfulness; first, pointing to what the sūtras say. The Tathāgata's text on the three foundations of mindfulness should be understood in its characteristics as taught in the sūtras.
Second, briefly revealing the meaning. Throughout the long night, the Tathāgatas hold this aspiration: that beings of every kind might truthfully dwell within the undistorted practice of the well-taught dharma and discipline. As the master of dharma holding this aspiration across the long night while guiding his assembly, whether his hopes are fulfilled or not, no defilement arises; this is briefly revealed by the three foundations of mindfulness.
Third, explaining their establishment; first, stating. These three foundations of mindfulness are further established according to three distinct assemblies.
Second, posing the question. What are these three assemblies?
Third, listing them. Those who, in their entirety, practice correctly are the first assembly; those who, in their entirety, practice wrongly are the second assembly; those among whom some practice correctly and some wrongly are the third assembly.

items.title: Section: The Three Things Requiring No Guarding — A Purity So Complete It Needs No Watching Over

items.zh: 如來所有三不護文，如契經說應知其相。謂諸如來以要言之，於一切種鄙惡所作覆藏永斷，由三不護之所顯示。諸阿羅漢由忘念故，於時時間片有無記鄙惡所作，如來於此一切一切皆無所有。是故如來於諸弟子，如所立要，即如自性切切誡勗，顯顯呵擯，時復現行率爾敦逼，於諸弟子無所防慮。所謂勿彼共住多時，知我所行三業不淨，因於前事意懷不悅，由斯不順乃事乖違，或面譏我，或向他說。
items.en:
Sixth, the three things requiring no guarding; first, pointing to what the sūtras say. The Tathāgata's text on the three things requiring no guarding should be understood as taught in the sūtras.
Second, revealing the essential meaning. In brief, the Tathāgatas have permanently severed every kind of concealment of unwholesome deeds; this is revealed by the three things requiring no guarding.
Third, distinguishing what is not shared; first, distinguishing the trace of unwholesomeness still present. Due to lapses of mindfulness, arhats may still, from time to time, exhibit some slight, morally neutral unwholesome trace; the Tathāgatas are entirely free of this in every respect.
Second, explaining the absence of concealment. Therefore the Tathāgata, towards his disciples, earnestly urges them according to the standard he himself has established, openly rebuking or expelling as needed, immediately correcting any relapse, entirely without private concern — never worrying that prolonged association might reveal impure conduct of his own, nor that a disciple, displeased by some prior matter, might grow resentful, act contrary to his wishes, criticise him to his face, or speak of it to others.

items.title: Section: Great Compassion Recalled, Never Forgetting a Single Task, and the Ninth Quality Opens

items.zh: 當知如來所有大悲一切種相，皆悉如前供養親近無量品說。當知如是如來大悲無量無上。云何如來無忘失法？謂諸如來常隨記念，若事、若處、若如、若時有所為作，如來即於此事、此處、此如、此時皆正隨念，是名如來無忘失法。所謂如來普於一切所作事業，普於一切方處差別，普於一切所作方便，普於一切時分差別，念無忘失，常住正念，當知是名無忘失法。云何如來永害習氣？
items.en:
Seventh, great compassion; first, pointing to what was said before. Know that every aspect of the Tathāgata's great compassion is as already explained in the earlier chapter on immeasurables, within offering and drawing near.
Second, revealing its unsurpassed nature. Know that the Tathāgata's great compassion is thus immeasurable and unsurpassed.
Eighth, the dharma of never forgetting; first, posing the question. What is the Tathāgata's dharma of never forgetting?
Second, explaining; first, stating the essential meaning. The Tathāgatas constantly and correctly recollect whatever task, place, method, or time is involved in what is to be done; with respect to that task, place, method, and time, correct recollection is always present; this is called the dharma of never forgetting.
Second, explaining the distinctions. The Tathāgata, universally with respect to every task, every place, every method, and every distinction of time, recollects without forgetting, abiding constantly in correct mindfulness; know this is called the dharma of never forgetting.
Ninth, the permanent destruction of habitual tendencies; first, posing the question. What is the Tathāgata's permanent destruction of habitual tendencies?

items.title: Section: Not a Trace, Even in Walking or Glancing — The Permanent Destruction of Habitual Tendencies, and Three Heaps of Dharma Opening the Final Quality

items.zh: 謂諸如來或於動轉、或於瞻視、或於言論、或於安住，似有煩惱所起作業多不現行，是名如來永害習氣。諸阿羅漢雖斷煩惱，而於動轉、瞻視、言論及安住中，而有種種似有煩惱所起作業。云何如來一切種妙智？謂諸如來以要言之，於三聚法現等正覺。何等為三？一者、能引有義聚法，二者、能引無義聚法，三者、非能引有義聚法非能引無義聚法。
items.en:
Second, explaining; first, stating the essential meaning. The Tathāgatas, whether in movement, gazing, speech, or dwelling, exhibit no conduct resembling what affliction produces; this is called the permanent destruction of habitual tendencies.
Second, distinguishing from the trainingless. Although arhats have severed affliction, they may still exhibit various conduct resembling what affliction produces, in movement, gazing, speech, and dwelling.
Tenth, wisdom of every kind; first, posing the question. What is the Tathāgata's wisdom of every kind?
Second, explaining; first, presenting the essential meaning; first, stating. In brief, the Tathāgatas manifest complete awakening with respect to three heaps of dharma.
Second, posing the question. What are these three?
Third, listing them. First, the heap of dharmas leading towards the meaningful; second, the heap of dharmas leading towards the meaningless; third, what leads towards neither the meaningful nor the meaningless.

blocks.text: More qualities unique to a buddha: equanimity towards every kind of disciple, a purity that needs no guarding, and the destruction even of habitual traces.

"He finds no genuine basis in the objections." Venerable Miào Jìng: no true reason supports the slander. Master Cháng Bǎi: sensual desire obstructs the path of cultivation, not the path of seeing; so a stream-enterer may still have a spouse.

The first two praise self-benefit, the latter two the benefit of others. They are taught for bodhisattvas; Master Cháng Bǎi, to guide them towards buddhahood. Venerable Miào Jìng: the compilers of scripture left out a phrase mentioning bodhisattvas, though the Buddha's intent was universal.

Towards disciples practising wholly correctly, wholly wrongly, and mixed. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha isn't pleased by obedience nor upset by disobedience. Master Cháng Bǎi: no elation at the obedient, no resentment of those who go wrong.
All concealment is severed. Venerable Miào Jìng: doing no evil, there is nothing to hide. Arhats may lapse slightly; the Tathāgata does not.
Master Cháng Bǎi: 如 here means the means, the methods by which a matter comes about.

Arhats have cut affliction, yet conduct resembling it remains. Master Cháng Bǎi: morally neutral, occasional, from habit. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha abides non-discriminatingly at all times, so this does not happen. The three heaps: Master Cháng Bǎi, good, evil, and neutral.
The traditional examples of an arhat's leftover habits are small: a hurried step, a sharp word from old custom. Only in a buddha are even these gone.

quiz.q: Why can the Tathāgata remain entirely self-assured?
options: he finds no genuine basis in any objection
quiz.why: He finds no genuine basis in the objections. Venerable Miào Jìng: no true reason supports the slander.

quiz.q: The Buddha says desire obstructs the path, yet stream-enterers still have desire. How is this resolved?
options: desire obstructs the path of cultivation, not seeing; innate craving is cut in cultivation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: desire obstructs the path of cultivation, not seeing. Venerable Miào Jìng agrees.

quiz.q: Why exactly four, and how do they map?
options: first two: benefit of self complete; last two: benefit of others
quiz.why: The first two praise self-benefit, the latter two benefit of others.

quiz.q: For whom does the Tathāgata praise his direct awakening?
options: bodhisattvas progressing towards the Great Vehicle
quiz.why: For bodhisattvas. Master Cháng Bǎi: to guide them towards buddhahood. Venerable Miào Jìng, of the other two vehicles: removing craving and views suffices.

quiz.q: "Omitted the bodhisattva's own words." How do the lectures take 菩薩言?
options: the word "bodhisattva" in the phrase; the śrāvaka canon drops it; the Buddha's intent is universal
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: there was a phrase with "bodhisattva," which they did not include; the Buddha's intent is universal. "Own words" could mislead.

quiz.q: On which three assemblies are the three foundations established?
options: wholly correct, wholly wrong, and mixed
quiz.why: Those practising wholly correctly, wholly wrongly, and those mixed.

quiz.q: What do the three foundations show, says Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: neither delight at obedience nor displeasure at disobedience; undefiled mindfulness
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha isn't pleased by obedience nor upset by disobedience; he abides in mindfulness regardless of circumstances.

quiz.q: How is the Buddha's mind towards each kind of disciple, per the lectures?
options: Miào Jìng: non-discriminating abiding towards all three; Cháng Bǎi: unelated by the correct, unresentful of the wrong
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: non-discriminating abiding towards all three. Master Cháng Bǎi: no elation at the obedient, no resentment of the wrong-doers.

quiz.q: What do the three non-guardings reveal, and how does the Buddha differ from arhats?
options: all concealment of unwholesome deeds severed; arhats have slight lapses, the Tathāgata none
quiz.why: All concealment is severed. Venerable Miào Jìng: doing no evil, there is nothing to hide. Arhats may lapse slightly; the Tathāgata does not.

quiz.q: The English renders 如 as "method." How do the lectures explain it?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 如 means means, various methods. Venerable Miào Jìng: means, how the matter comes about. The English "method" fits.

quiz.q: Here the English says "exhibit no conduct" for 多不現行. How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the destruction of habits?
options: the Buddha abides non-discriminatingly at all times, so it doesn't occur and he doesn't habituate
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha abides non-discriminatingly at all times, so this doesn't happen and he doesn't habituate. The English renders the same phrase "no conduct" here and "mostly" at §21.

quiz.q: How do arhats stand regarding habitual tendencies?
options: though afflictions are severed, conduct resembling them remains
quiz.why: Arhats have cut affliction yet conduct resembling it remains. Master Cháng Bǎi: morally neutral, occasional, from habit.

quiz.q: In which three heaps does the Tathāgata awaken, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi map them?
options: leading to the meaningful, the meaningless, neither; good, evil, neutral
quiz.why: The heaps leading to the meaningful, the meaningless, and neither. Master Cháng Bǎi: good, evil, and neutral.
